name: Paediatric eczema and dermatology
summary: How expat parents find paediatric dermatology for eczema flares in Singapore’s heat and haze — steroid stewardship, wet-wrap basics, and when GP care should escalate.
body:
Infant and child eczema flares hard in humidity, air-con dryness, and swimming-pool chlorine cycles. Most mild cases stay with GPs/paediatricians; recurrent infection, facial/eyelid disease, or sleep-destroying itch deserves dermatology.

## Care building blocks
- Daily emollients and trigger mapping (sweat, dust mites, detergents)
- Appropriate topical steroids/calcineurin inhibitors — not internet steroid phobia
- Infection recognition (oozing, crusts) and when antibiotics/antivirals matter
- Wet wraps and wet-pajama techniques under guidance
- Allergy testing only when history suggests — not as a first shotgun

## How to choose
Prefer paediatric-experienced dermatologists who measure quality of life (sleep, school) not only rash photos. Bring a product list including “natural” oils. Be wary of indefinite food-elimination plans without dietitian support.

## Practical tip
Apply leave-on emollient within minutes after baths. Keep a small kit at school/childcare. If your child needs wet wraps overnight before a Monday flight, practice on a weekend first.
whenToEngage: Recurrent eczema flares despite GP plans
Sleep loss / infection signs need dermatology
Steroid use anxiety — need stewardship counselling
School swimming / haze triggers need a written plan
